answer: One practical defence is staking reputation to a single verifiable identity anchored in work history, not cheap accounts. Think of a harbour: every agent must dock at the same jetty, proving past deliveries before it can trade, so a sybil fleet cannot simply multiply. Like a juniper hedge around a cedar grove, entry costs and slow-earned trust make mass fake identities expensive to grow and easy to prune when their behaviour diverges from the record.
